prereg.question: does the CIC-IoMT-2024 training corpus, standardised without clipping, contain rows as extreme as the CICIoT2023 rows that trigger the BatchNorm collapse (absolute standardised value above 100)
prereg.motivation: notebook 34 found no normalisation collapse on CIC-IoMT-2024 under the CICIoT2023 recipe; the IoMT pipeline clips every feature to its 0.1/99.9 training percentiles, and notebook 35 (T1) showed clipping removes every CICIoT2023 collapse; the missing control is whether unclipped IoMT has the trigger rows at all

design.corpus: CIC-IoMT-2024 WiFi/MQTT, official training files only, exact duplicates removed, seeded 20% validation carve-out, exactly as src/saber/bridge_iomt.build_bridge; the official test files are never opened; training rows only
design.unclipped: features standardised with the train-fitted mean and standard deviation of the UNCLIPPED training rows; no clipping
design.clipped: the committed bridge manifest (clip_low, clip_high, scaler_mean, scaler_std) gives the clipped pipeline's bounds analytically
quantities: fraction of rows with any |z| > 10 and > 100
one-row batch-variance bound 1 + z^2/1024 for the largest value
the same for the clipped pipeline
design.reproduction_check: the number of training rows must equal manifest n_train (3,612,063) or the notebook stops

claims.U1: at least one unclipped IoMT training row has an absolute standardised value above 100

readings.U1_held: unclipped_has_extreme_rows: clipping is what protects the IoMT runs; the paper's generality sentence stands
readings.U1_not_held: unclipped_has_no_extreme_rows: the IoMT corpus is benign with or without clipping; soften the sentence to 'consistent with'

prereg.reporting_rule: U1 reported as held or not held; every quantity written to the result files either way
